title: Entrance Fee Amount on the Closing-Year Tax Letter by How the Entrance Fee Agreement Ended
content:
The entrance fee amount the closing-year tax letter of an **Entrance Fee Agreement** rests on depends on how the agreement ended: where it terminated after occupancy, by the resident's death, the resident's notice or Larkspur for cause, with the termination date in the closing year, the amount is the administrative retention and the amortization entries posted in the closing year; where it was rescinded or cancelled before occupancy in the closing year, the amount is 0; otherwise it is the entrance fee received in the closing year.

The entrance fee share of the letter is the plan's entrance fee medical expense percentage of that entrance fee amount.

The closing year is the span of 1 to 12 whole months before the January issue date (at least 1 and fewer than 13 whole months). The termination reason and the termination date are those on the agreement record.

## Ending table

| How the agreement ended | Termination date in the closing year | Entrance fee amount |
|---|---|---|
| Death, resident's notice or Larkspur for cause (after occupancy) | Yes | Administrative retention plus amortization entries posted in the closing year |
| Rescission, or cancellation before occupancy (resident's cancellation or death or illness) | Yes | 0 |
| Any ending | No | Entrance fee received in the closing year |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- Terminated on the resident's death on 18 June; occupancy began years earlier; six amortization entries of 5113.50 were posted in the closing year and no administrative retention: entrance fee amount 30681.00.
- Occupancy and termination by notice both in the closing year: administrative retention of 13636.00 and amortization entries of 20454.00 give 34090.00.
- Cancelled before occupancy in the closing year after a deposit of 34090.00: entrance fee amount 0.
